lesson.title: Which parts are equal?
lesson.subtitle: Use equal-whole pictures
lesson.story: Three same-sized rectangles are divided in different ways. Study the size of each part.
lesson.objective: Recognise equal-area parts of one whole.

steps.title: Find equal parts
steps.prompt: Which rectangle is divided into equal parts?
hints: Look at how much of the whole each part covers.
Compare the widths of the parts in each rectangle.
With the same height, equal widths make equal areas.
Using the whole picture, choose Rectangle B.

steps.title: Count equal parts
steps.prompt: How many equal parts are in that rectangle?
hints: Look carefully at the whole picture.
Count the parts in the picture.
Separate the number of shaded parts from the number of all parts.
Count in the picture: there are 4 equal parts in the whole.

steps.title: Count shaded parts
steps.prompt: How many of its equal parts are shaded?
hints: Look carefully at the whole picture.
Count the parts in the picture.
Separate the number of shaded parts from the number of all parts.
Count in the picture: there are 1 shaded parts.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: What must we check before naming or comparing these fractions?

choices.label: Count the shaded parts, even if the parts are different sizes.
Check that the parts are equal and the wholes are the same size.
A fraction with a bigger denominator is always the bigger one.

hints: Think about what a fraction describes.
Each part must have the same area.
Comparison also needs the same-sized whole.
Check that the parts are equal and the wholes are the same size.
